rationale: A case-insensitive script over this app's BSB finds "mustard seed" in Matthew only at 13:31 and 17:20 (and in the other Gospels at Mark 4:31, Luke 13:19 and Luke 17:6); the Greek is kokkos sinapeos in both Matthew verses in all nine editions Bible Hub lists. At 13:31-32 the seed is "the smallest of all seeds" that "grows into the largest of garden plants"; at 17:20 it is the measure of a faith that could say "to this mountain, 'Move from here to there.'" Motif/strong on the precedent of conn-matt16-leaven-matt13: a rare image recurring within one Gospel, in the same words. The row grades the recurrence, not a meaning. Readers differ on what the seed stands for at 17:20: Ellicott calls it "the proverbial type of the infinitely little" and the Expositor's Greek Testament "a minimum of faith," while Barnes reports a reading that stresses "increasing, expanding, enlarged faith" and calls it "probably the true meaning" (all via Bible Hub). Origen joins the two passages, saying such faith "becomes a great tree" (Commentary on Matthew XIII).
